A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Boost-and-Skip research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, ablations, computational measurements, and downstream classification results in Tables 1–6 and the accompanying main-text and appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, component and frequency-filtering ablations, and classification experiments using generated training data.

M1.justification: The variance-boosted initialization and timestep-skipping procedure in Section 3.2, including Equations 10–12, is unchanged. The small wording edit to the timestep-skipping description does not alter the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the concentric-circle toy data, CelebA 64×64, LSUN-Bedrooms 256×256, and ImageNet at 64×64 and 256×256. The unconditional and class-conditional generation tasks and downstream CelebA attribute-classification experiment are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same dataset-specific comparator rows, including ADM, the relevant GAN/LDM/EDM/DiT/CADS baselines, guided minority samplers, and temperature sampling. Comparator membership in the downstream experiment and appendix figures is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same metrics, reference-data selection, 30,000 generated evaluation samples, hyperparameters, and sampling budgets of 250 timesteps for comparisons and 100 for analyses. The downstream augmentation and testing procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations in Table 2, trajectory analyses in Figures 2–4, frequency-filtering study in Table 5, and reduced-variance study in Table 6. Appendix D retains the same neighborhood distributions and qualitative comparisons.

E5.justification: Table 4 reports averages over three runs in both versions, and Figure 5 retains the shared-random-seed comparison. There are no additions or revisions to run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the result figures retain the same numerical and qualitative findings. For example, Boost-and-Skip's ImageNet 64×64 cFID remains 12.68, its inference time remains 0.98 seconds/sample, and downstream classification accuracy remains 0.902.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propositions, corollary, and assumptions in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same proofs and derivations; equations moving across page boundaries are layout changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: two simple sampling modifications enable competitive minority generation with lower computational costs, supported by theory and downstream augmentation results. No scientific contribution is added, strengthened, or narrowed.

C2.justification: The low-density-emphasis and stochastic-contraction explanations remain unchanged, as do the deterministic-sampler limitation and Appendix A's quality–diversity interpretation. The Impact Statement retains the same concern about suppressing minority features through reduced initialization variance.

D1.justification: Appendix C changes the listed GitHub repository from anonymous7172/BnS to soobin-um/BnS, and v2 also places the updated address in the abstract. Implementation, model-source, hyperparameter, and hardware details are otherwise unchanged; the PDFs do not establish changes to the repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in the introduction and Appendix A.1 are unchanged. The references reflow following the added acknowledgments, without additions or removals of cited research.

P1.justification: v2 corrects the spelling of 'amplifying,' shortens the timestep-skipping wording, adds funding acknowledgments, and replaces the preprint notice with ICML proceedings information. The scientific narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded abstract, proceedings notice, and acknowledgments produce modest column and page reflow, including shifted equation and reference placement. All eleven figures and six tables retain their content, captions, and display structure.

improvement.justification: v2 offers minor editorial polish and makes the updated code address easier to find, but v1 already supplied a repository link. The methods, theoretical support, experiments, results, and limitations are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These small presentation and attribution updates do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement.
